title: An Atomically Thin Protective Layer for High-Temperature Oxidation Shielding of Metals
content: The susceptibility of metals such as copper (Cu), nickel (Ni), and iron (Fe) to oxidation poses a significant obstacle to their wider application, especially in demanding environments where elevated temperatures or corrosive species accelerate the degradation process. Conventional strategies [1-3], such as coatings, alloying, and electroplating, often prove insufficient due to the inherent ability of oxygen (O), with its small size, to infiltrate and diffuse within the metal lattice. Recent research has demonstrated the potential of solvothermal treatment to induce crystallographic reconstruction of copper surfaces for achieving passivated Cu capable of resisting oxidation [4]. Despite this advancement, maintaining the surface stability of metals at elevated temperatures without compromising their intrinsic properties remains a challenge.
